A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Linear-Core Surrogates work. The main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 noise experiments, synthetic optimization and sequence-tagging experiments, and a Penn Treebank timing comparison in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds a BERT-based sequence-tagging timing comparison in Section 5.5.

M1.justification: New Appendix K proposes expanding sequence-model states to encode n-gram histories and constructing sampling proposals over weighted finite-state transducer paths. This is a limited methodological adaptation for non-decomposable metrics; the established losses and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, and the adaptation is not experimentally demonstrated.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same binary problems, corrupted CIFAR-10, synthetic sequence tagging and artificially expanded Penn Treebank tagging task. BERT changes the model configuration, not the represented task or data. Appendix K mentions F1 and BLEU without evaluating them.

E2.justification: Section 5.5 adds an evaluated BERT-CRF comparator against BERT-Linear-Core alongside the retained BiLSTM comparison. The Cross-Entropy, Generalized Cross-Entropy, Hinge and Structured SVM comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added BERT comparison uses AdamW while retaining the 4,000-tag task, batch size 8, sequence-length filter and 83% accuracy target. Appendix E's convergence-plot caption changes from 10 to 200 labels, resolving its disagreement with the setup already stated in v1; this does not establish that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The new comparison across BiLSTM and BERT explicitly tests whether the efficiency advantage persists across encoders and whether the bottleneck resides in the structured loss layer. Existing gradient-distribution, optimization-stability and core-threshold analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental run counts, seeds or significance tests. Existing shaded scalability plots are retained without new uncertainty definitions, and the BERT comparison adds no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Section 5.5 and Figure 8 newly report 78.7 seconds for BERT-CRF versus 5.1 seconds for BERT-Linear-Core to reach 83% accuracy, a reported 15.4-fold speedup. These are additional results under a new backbone configuration. Table 2, the BiLSTM timings and the retained appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix K adds an informal mathematical argument that a history-expanded transducer representation preserves linear consistency, bounded variance and computational efficiency for non-decomposable metrics. It supplies no complete derivation. Existing theorem statements and proofs remain unchanged; the variance theorem is merely renumbered from 5.2 to 5.3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion newly assert priority as the first explicit smooth surrogate family with linear H-consistency across the three settings. V1's explicit energy-saving claims disappear. The central consistency, robustness and computational-efficiency contributions otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the BERT results as locating the computational bottleneck strictly in the structured loss layer and broadens claimed applicability to exact F1 and BLEU in Appendix K. Appendix A also expands the explanation of how zero core curvature avoids the cited square-root barrier. These extensions receive no corresponding new limitations discussion.

D1.justification: V2 identifies AdamW for the new BERT experiment and corrects the CRF transition-interaction description from 4000 × 400 to 4000 × 4000. Existing implementation settings remain largely unchanged; the exact BERT configuration, timing hardware and code access information are not supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix A now explicitly identifies Cao et al.'s binary loss as a special case of the Linear-Core family, rather than merely structurally similar, and expands discussion of the universal square-root result. References are added for rational kernels, BERT, AdamW and further consistency research; the main prior-work relationships remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution roadmap, conclusion and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten around a theory-first progression through binary, multi-class and structured prediction. Appendix A becomes a numbered comparison, and new Remark 5.2 consolidates the rate comparisons. The main section sequence is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with reversed-margin standard losses and revised axes and legends. V1's appendix loss-surface figure moves into the main text as Figure 3. The combined efficiency figure is split, with a new BERT panel added. Other figures and tables are chiefly relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The BERT comparison adds limited support for the efficiency claim, while the corrected label-count caption, clearer prior-work discussion and removal of unmeasured energy-saving claims improve precision. These gains are tempered by Appendix K's broad exact-F1/BLEU guarantees without a complete derivation or evaluation. The established proofs and experimental findings remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is modest.
